newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end weaker after losses pared.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end weaker after losses pared.

text.p: FCOJ futures ended weaker Friday but were able to claw their way back from some of the selling.
Celeste Georgakis of Dean Witter said the market was still ignoring reports of canker and Medflies in Florida.
"The market does not really give them much importance," Georgakis said.
Most-active July juice settled 0.80 cent lower at 76.20 cents a lb, traded 77.10 to 75.25 cents. Volume was estimated at 5,500 lots compared with Thursday's official tally of 3,121 lots.

Analyst Judith Ganes of Merrill Lynch said fundamentals are unchanged. "There simply could be too much juice in the season ahead following record output this year," she added in her Citrus Weekly report.

The futures market reflects the reality of oversupply yet overpayment for fruit has probably kept processors from lowering prices and this in turn has prevented retail prices from dropping and demand from turning upwards, Ganes said.
